newsitem.title: UK: Russian debt up on local buying, Brazil up on vote.
newsitem.headline: Russian debt up on local buying, Brazil up on vote.

text.p: Brady bonds prices were mixed on Friday ahead of the U.S. jobs report due later today, but Russian dollar loans were sharply higher on local buying and Brazilian debt prices were firmer on passage of the re-election amendment.

"The market is fairly strong today. But I am surprised we have seen the amount (of activity) we have so far" in advance of the U.S. employment report, a Brady bond trader at a major U.S. investment bank in London said.

Russian Vnesheconombank dollar loans posted the biggest gains, up 7/8 at 89-1/8, as continued improvement in the country's economic fundamentals prompted local buyers to enter the market. "In Russia, some good numbers were released and because of that there has been one good local buyer who tried to push the price up this morning. We closed at 88-3/4, it (Russian dollar Vnesh) traded up to 89-5/8 and now it settled at 89-1/8," an emerging market trader said.

In Brazil, prices continued to move higher on the success of the $3 billion 30-year bond deal and passage of the re-election amendment that would allow President Fernando Henrique Cardoso to run for a second term. But one market expert said further upside on Brazilian debt instruments may now be somewhat limited.

"My argument is that Brazil has seen a lot of good news and quite a rally therefore how much more upside is there relative to the others'" said Richard Gray, emerging market analyst at BankAmerica in London.
Still, Brazilian discount bonds were 1/8 firmer at 83-3/4 bid and its par bonds were 1/8 stronger at 66-3/4 bid.
Among other Latin Brady instruments, Venezuelan Brady bonds were lower on profittaking after posting sharp gains on news of a ratings upgrade by Standard and Poor's Corp on Thursday.
Venezuelan FLIRBS were one percentage point lower at 91 bid after rising 1-1/2 on Thursday to 92-1/2.
S&P upgraded the country's long-term foreign currency rating to B-plus from B.
Elsewhere, market expert ssaid they were awaiting the latest U.S. jobs figures due to be released at 1230 GMT.
